en: Students paste AI answers into homework every day. The answers sound sure, even when a date or a name is wrong. Receipts checks an AI answer claim by claim, in your browser, with no account and no key.

This is a real ChatGPT answer from a public research dataset. Receipts splits it into small claims, finds Wikipedia sentences that could back each one, and a small language model running in the browser reads them.
ChatGPT says she was born in 1893. Wikipedia says 1892. Receipts marks it contradicted, and shows you the exact sentence, with a link, so you can decide.

Here is the problem we had to beat. Give the raw model an unrelated sentence about a river, and it often calls that a contradiction. A naive fact checker would tell you a true fact is false. Our relevance gate says: no receipt.

We measured this on public, human-labelled data. On seven hundred and twelve test pairs, the raw model called unrelated text a contradiction most of the time; with the gate, it answers no receipt almost always. On real ChatGPT answers, when Receipts says backed, human annotators mostly agree.
It works beyond biographies too. In this paragraph we planted one mistake: the year the Eiffel Tower was completed. No receipt does not mean false. It means: check this one yourself.
No training, pretrained models only, tested code, and every number is in the repository. Receipts: ask the AI for its receipts.
